scope.database: PostgreSQL 18, pinned psycopg 3.3.6, synchronous unnamed tuple cursors
scope.table: exactly id text PRIMARY KEY and value integer NOT NULL before installation
scope.keys: 1..64 distinct existing text keys, at most 512 UTF-8 bytes each; the declared set exactly covers the locked initial row set
sql: generated point UPDATE without business RETURNING

initialization: Require dedicated idle autocommit setup, PG18 and standard tuple rows.
Begin, ACCESS EXCLUSIVE-lock the business table before catalog checks or migration; reject unsafe inherited/FK/rule/check/generated/custom-type/index features and wrong column shape.
Reuse the frozen column prototype DDL and verify_installation exactly, never instantiate its CaptureSession or inherit its _events.
Read actual key/value/server-token rows under the same installation/verification lock; at most64 rows; do not initialize from later reads.
Acknowledge COMMIT before publishing one v3 initial snapshot or permitting business wrappers. Initialization errors preserve rollback uncertainty and prevent wrapping.
observations: Only actual delivered positive SELECT rows produce read facts; a later EOF produces no duplicate fact. A fetchmany request returning no rows before actual exhaustion is not EOF.

Observed UPDATE returns the actual PG18 OLD/NEW token generated by the installed BEFORE trigger. Every intermediate write is retained, including repeated business values. Predecessors are metadata, never fabricated SELECT reads.

For original UPDATE without RETURNING, consume only internal observer rows, keep business description/rownumber=None, original rowcount/statusmessage, and pinned driver's no-result fetch class/message. These synthetic no-result exceptions are distinguished from actual driver exceptions rethrown by identity.
Internal command result rows go to a separate bounded source JSONL with statement/business-rows event references; they are never emitted as business rows or an unapproved v3 effectRows transport.

Unknown SQL, bad scope parameters or unsupported factories execute the original business query and record explicit coverage gaps. Installation restricts some unsupported writes: no zero-change/transparent arbitrary-SQL claim.
Business exceptions from original execute/fetch/commit/rollback remain the same exception object. Observer failures add gaps rather than changing the business return.

budgets.journal: reuse existing bounded SegmentedJournal defaults; no _events or whole-log history list

ledger: Run only after all business workers stop and wrappers are closed/idle, in a dedicated setup transaction holding the table lock.
Verify installed ownership/catalog again and use an actual server cursor; client fetchmany alone on a normal PGresult is not a streaming-memory claim.
Write each actual audit row and source query identity to bounded source JSONL; do not infer commit order from UUID, ACK, clocks or database sequence.
A row/error/byte budget exhaustion produces an explicit gap and incomplete footer; do not silently truncate then declare a complete ledger.
This first slice streams the small actual ledger, not a scalable warmup/window lineage filter. No 4096-key/60-second cost eligibility is claimed.

handoff.implementation: design and bounded admission checks only in this slice; automatic handoff is not implemented
futureProtocol: Explicit caller quiescence plus actual no active/unknown transactions, no pending-result identities and no prior gaps; require every old business connection actually closed.
Under the same setup lock, verify source metadata and obtain actual final tokens and bounded streaming ledger; seal old journal/source-log and bind their exact hashes.

Persist a handoff intent before sealing; create a new observer epoch and locked actual initial snapshot, acknowledge setup commit, publish a completed chain record, then return fresh wrappers. Do not reuse old wrappers transparently.

A failed or incomplete handoff record makes the multi-window stream incomplete; an old valid bounded window is not proof of complete continuous capture. Old-wrapper post-close activity retains existing persistent invalidation semantics.

proofAndCost.futureProtocol: 15s warmup/60s starts/<=30s drain, 3 ABC-BCA-CAB batches, column+sidecar, all attempts/errors/gaps/durable tail/CPU/RSS/WAL/lock samples retained; not executed by this draft
